summary.text: Veronica Fernandez is a Morris County small-business owner and former insurance underwriter running as the End the Corruption! Party nominee, campaigning primarily on campaign-finance reform. She has run for office several times, including the 2020 U.S. Senate race and a 2023 General Assembly race.

paragraphs.text: Fernandez was born and raised in Franklin, New Jersey, and earned a high school diploma from Sussex County Vo-Tech before attending County College of Morris. She lives in Long Valley, Morris County, and, according to WHYY, is married with two children.
She worked for 20 years as a licensed property/casualty and health insurance underwriter in New Jersey.

Fernandez co-owns and operates a small commercial electrical contracting business with her husband, a Navy veteran and electrician, and in her survey response she describes experience owning and operating a union (IBEW Local 102) shop.

She was volunteer coordinator for the Interfaith Council of Homeless Families in Morris County for seven years and a foster parent, according to her survey response, and Ballotpedia notes an affiliation with the League of Women Voters.

Fernandez ran for U.S. Senate in 2020 as the Of, By, For! Party candidate (0.7%), withdrew from the 2022 race for New Jersey's 7th Congressional District, and ran for New Jersey General Assembly District 24 in 2023 as the End The Corruption! Party candidate (8.1%).
She told WHYY that campaign finance reform is essential and that she supports efforts to overturn the Supreme Court's decision in Citizens United v. FEC.
